entries.subject: NASA VTAD WASP-12b 3D model texture as an illustration lens
entries.finding: Not shown. NASA's WASP-12b 3D Model (WASP-12b_1_249888.glb) is egg-shaped, as the planet is stretched by its star: semi-axes 640, 449 and 480 units, centred 62 units off its origin, 6.5% from the best-fitting centred ellipsoid where the illustration route allows 1%. Its texture coordinates are not the mesh's own longitude and latitude (median 5 degrees, up to 19 degrees apart), so no placement on the published sphere keeps NASA's texels where the model puts them. The base-colour texture is named JupiterColor_orange_w_hotspot.jpg: a recoloured Jupiter with a hot spot.

entries.subject: Bell et al. (2019) Spitzer 3.6 um first-order fits of 2010 and 2013, as two maps of longitude
entries.finding: Shown as two temperature lenses through the Cowan & Agol (2008) inversion, one per visit, each legend naming the other. Table A2 fiducial (PLD, first order) rows: 2010 C1 0.371, D1 -0.239, F_day 3870 ppm, R_p/R_* 0.11642; 2013 C1 0.320, D1 0.079, F_day 3840 ppm, R_p/R_* 0.11327. With the star at the value each row's day side implies (6,033 and 6,031 K), the night sides come out 1,525 and 1,757 K against 1,510 +/- 210 and 1,760 +/- 97 K, and the peaks 32.8 degrees before and 13.9 degrees after eclipse against 32.6 +/- 6.2 and -13.6 +/- 3.8. Appendix B prints 5,800 K at 3.6 um, which would give a 2,668 K day side for 2010, not the table's 2,744 K; the 3.6 and 4.5 um values appear swapped in the text.

entries.subject: The 4.5 um phase curves of Cowan et al. (2012) and Bell et al. (2019), with their strong second-order terms
entries.finding: Both 4.5 um visits need a second-order sinusoid (Bell et al. 2019, Table A2: C2 -0.252 and -0.307) that the paper attributes to gas flowing off the planet along the star-planet line, not to the planet's heat; its temperatures use the first-order terms alone. A Cowan & Agol map of the full curve would paint that gas onto the planet, and a first-order-only map would drop a fitted term, so neither is drawn. Cowan et al. (2012) fit the same 2010 visit with a thermal sinusoid plus an ellipsoidal cos 2alpha term (Table 3: 2A_therm, alpha_max, A_ellips).
entries.revisitWhen: A paper separates the planet's 4.5 um map from the gas signal.

entries.subject: Dang et al. (2025) SPCA reanalysis of both 4.5 um visits
entries.finding: Visit 1 offset -8 +5/-4 degrees east, day side 2,900 +/- 100 K, night side 1,100 +/- 200 K; visit 2 offset 30 +/- 8 degrees east, 3,000 +/- 100 K, 1,500 +200/-300 K (Tables 2 and 3 of arXiv v1). It also finds the visits disagree. It prints fluxes, offsets and temperatures but not its Fourier coefficients, so its curves cannot be drawn without refitting.
entries.revisitWhen: Its fit coefficients or model curves are published.
